claim: The three locomoting canonical Pelagos fauna families now have anatomy-driven armature foundations and explicit collision/query intent. Coral escriba is intentionally kept static/procedural because deformation is not justified by its current gameplay role.

PEL-ECO-JELLY-001.policy: bell contraction + six oral-arm chains + twelve sensory-tentacle chains
PEL-ECO-JELLY-001.collision: non-blocking bell overlap/query sphere proposal; tentacles have no solid collider

PEL-ECO-EEL-001.policy: anguilliform axial chain derived from authored body-segment centers
PEL-ECO-EEL-001.collision: three non-blocking overlap/query segment proxies; solid blocking remains gameplay-dependent

PEL-ECO-BOV-001.policy: root/spine/head plus six three-bone limb chains for reef-grazing locomotion
PEL-ECO-BOV-001.collision: simple torso + head compound blocking proposal; foot contact semantics pending engine

PEL-ECO-SCRIBE-001.rationale: Its canonical identity is recording vibration through growth. A deformation rig is not justified until an authored interaction requires it.
PEL-ECO-SCRIBE-001.collision: background non-blocking by default; hero interaction proxy TBD

reason_not_done: Skinning/deformation, locomotion animation, runtime behavior/physics, fauna LOD, engine collision semantics, performance and human GATE-ART remain open.
